stemMd: In a survey of $40$ commuters, $23$ say they use the bus, $19$ say they use the train and $6$ say they use neither. How many of the commuters use both the bus and the train?
explanationMd:
Start from the people who use **at least one** of the two services, because that is the set the bus and train counts describe between them.

Of the $40$ commuters, $6$ use neither, so $40 - 6 = 34$ use the bus, the train or both.

Adding the two counts, $23 + 19 = 42$, counts everyone who uses both services twice. The excess over the true union is exactly the overlap:

$$|\text{bus} \cap \text{train}| = 23 + 19 - 34 = 8$$

Check with the four regions of a Venn diagram: bus only $23 - 8 = 15$, train only $19 - 8 = 11$, both $8$, neither $6$. These add to $15 + 11 + 8 + 6 = 40$, the size of the survey.

The habit to keep: before using $|X \cup Y| = |X| + |Y| - |X \cap Y|$, make sure the union you plug in excludes anyone outside both sets.

distractorRationale.a: This is $23 + 19 - 40$: it uses the whole survey as the union, forgetting that $6$ commuters are in neither set. The union of bus users and train users has only $34$ members.
distractorRationale.b: This repeats the number of commuters who use neither service. That region lies outside both sets; the overlap is a different region of the diagram.
distractorRationale.d: This is the number who use the train only, $19 - 8$. It is one region of the correct diagram, reported instead of the overlap.
distractorRationale.e: This is the number who use the bus only, $23 - 8$. It answers "bus but not train" rather than "bus and train".

accessibilityText: A survey of 40 commuters: 23 use the bus, 19 use the train, 6 use neither. The question asks how many use both. The answer choices are the whole numbers 2, 6, 8, 11 and 15.

provenance.notes: Original item. Two-set inclusion-exclusion with a 'neither' group, numbers chosen so that each Venn region is a distinct distractor.
